expectations.text: Class comment states purpose and thread-safety guarantee
expectations.evidence: File comment: 'Thread safety: all public methods are safe to call concurrently'; class comment explains the lazy-refill design.

expectations.text: Every public method declaration has a contract comment
expectations.evidence: Constructor, Acquire, TryAcquire, AvailableTokens, and accessors all documented.

expectations.text: Acquire documents blocking; TryAcquire documents true/false and nothing-consumed-on-failure
expectations.evidence: Acquire documents blocking, capacity clamping, sleep-not-spin; TryAcquire: 'false if there were not enough tokens (bucket state is unchanged).'

expectations.text: Units documented for rates and durations
.cc explains implementation choices without duplicating .h contracts
expectations.evidence: No .h contract duplicated; .cc comments cover refill capping rationale, deficit-sleep computation, spurious wakeups.

expectations.text: No restating comments; no Author lines; consistent // style
expectations.evidence: Two comments restate adjacent code: 'return;  // Nothing to acquire.' and 'return true;  // Nothing to acquire; trivially succeeds.' Also uses Python-docstring-style 'Args:'/'Returns:' sections inside C++ comments and '// rate_limiter.h' filename headers — non-idiomatic for Google C++ prose comments.
Usage example uses /*capacity=*/100.0, /*refill_rate=*/50.0; no unannotated literal call sites.
